findings.claim: The comment says the test now holds on every page size, but only the past case is guarded against ARG_MAX. The under case sends about bound-1152 bytes of identifiers as sh arguments with no guard. With 64 KiB pages, as on some arm64 hosts, the bound is 2 MiB. With the usual 8 MiB stack limit, ARG_MAX is 2 MiB, so the exec of sh itself should fail with E2BIG. The same happens on any host where ARG_MAX is close to the bound, for example a small stack rlimit. Then the under case fails the test (exit and stdout mismatch) instead of being skipped or sized under ARG_MAX/2. I did not run this. It follows from the added arithmetic and the file's own comment that exec limits arguments and environment together.

The ENVIRON lint flags every occurrence of the word ENVIRON, including one in an awk comment or in a string, and the lint reads the whole script, not only the awk bodies. A future header or comment that mentions ENVIRON would fail the lint with a message about an unforced numeric read. This is a false-positive risk. No current line trips it, because the only ENVIRON in the script is at line 144. The bracketed-subscript row `ENVIRON[a[1]] ""` is also deliberately counted as unforced.
